entities.name: 'Alawi dynasty
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Alawi dynasty (Alaouite dynasty), founded in Morocco in 1631 when Moulay al-Sharif became the first Alawi Sultan of Tafilalt, is the reigning dynasty of the Kingdom of Morocco — the world's oldest continuously reigning royal family from Africa, ruling for 393+ years (longer than any European dynasty). The Alawis trace descent from the Prophet Muhammad through his grandson Hassan, giving the Moroccan monarchy its religious legitimacy (Commander of the Faithful — Amir al-Mu'minin). Morocco has never been colonized by a Muslim power and the Alawi dynasty represents an unbroken indigenous sovereignty.

The dynasty consolidated Moroccan sovereignty in the 17th-18th centuries, resisting Ottoman expansion while the rest of North Africa became Ottoman provinces — Morocco remains the only North African country that was never Ottoman-controlled. Sultan Muhammad III (r. 1757-1790) was the first foreign head of state to recognize the United States (1777), establishing the Morocco-US Treaty of Friendship (1786) — the oldest unbroken bilateral treaty in US history.

France established a protectorate over Morocco (1912-1956) but did not depose the Alawi sultans — instead ruling through them, then exiling Sultan Muhammad V (1953) after his nationalist stance, then restoring him (1955) as nationalist pressure grew. Muhammad V became King at independence (1956); Hassan II (r. 1961-1999) ruled Morocco through the Cold War 'Years of Lead' using emergency power. Muhammad VI (r. 1999-present) has pursued gradual liberalization. Morocco is the world's largest phosphate reserve holder and a major agricultural exporter.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Alawi dynasty — world's longest-ruling African dynasty, first to recognize the United States, and unique in resisting Ottoman expansion that absorbed all other North African states — represents the most durable non-European sovereignty in Africa and the first official international recognition of American independence.
